name: DaVinci Fusion Tracker And Magic Mask Graphics
use_when: Text, graphics, rectangles, heat signatures, or masks must follow camera or subject motion.
A graphic needs to sit behind or attach to a moving subject.
Resolve Studio Magic Mask is available and subject isolation is worth the review time.
avoid_when: The object does not move enough to justify tracking.
A static mask or simple keyframe would be clearer and faster.
Magic Mask edges are too unstable for the delivery size or subject importance.

timeline_pattern.pattern: Fusion -> Tracker_or_MagicMask -> track_forward_backward -> attach_graphic_or_mask -> refine_edges -> review_full_range
timeline_pattern.tracker_rule: Use Tracker Match Move when a graphic should follow a tracked feature.
timeline_pattern.foreground_rule: A tracked graphic can be generated foreground-only and merged later for cleaner control.
timeline_pattern.mask_reuse_rule: One tracked mask can drive multiple nodes through mask inputs when the same region controls several effects.
timeline_pattern.studio_rule: Magic Mask is Studio-only; keep a manual mask or simpler design fallback.

motion.rule: Track the most stable high-contrast feature available and check the attachment across the whole range.

keyframe_values.review_interval: Inspect at motion changes, occlusions, and the first/last frame of the affected range.
keyframe_values.edge_refinement: Use blur/erode/dilate only enough to hide edge chatter without shrinking important subject detail.

sound.rule: Only add tracking or reveal SFX when the attached graphic is an intentional emphasis beat.

captions.rule: Tracked graphics should not drag the viewer's eye away from required captions or cover the speaker's face.

color.rule: Tracked effects should match the grade and should not create halo edges after final color.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use external tracking/mask data when available; otherwise approximate with manually keyframed overlay positions and alpha masks.
implementation.remotion: Store tracked points or subject masks as frame-indexed metadata and drive overlay transforms from them.
implementation.blender: Use motion tracking, object tracking, masks, and compositor nodes for attached graphics or subject separation.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use motion tracking or keyframes for attached text; use cutout tools only after checking edges.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use mask tracking, position keyframes, or After Effects tracking/rotoscoping for more complex attachments.

common_mistakes: Tracking a weak feature that drifts as soon as the subject turns.
Trusting Magic Mask without edge and occlusion review.
Attaching graphics that cover the face, action, or captions.
Using a tracked effect where a static title would be calmer and clearer.
qc: Does the graphic or mask stay attached through the whole affected range?
Were occlusions, motion changes, and edge chatter reviewed?
Is there a non-Studio fallback if Magic Mask is unavailable?
Does the effect preserve faces, captions, proof, and action?
Does final color reveal any halos or rough mask edges?
